## Natural history notes

A native annual to short-lived perennial herb in the sunflower family, characterized by upright branching stems, broad alternate leaves, and clusters of small pinkish to purplish flower heads. Camphor-Weed has aromatic foliage that releases a strong camphor-like scent when crushed. In Florida, it occurs primarily in freshwater wetlands and other moist habitats, including swamps, wet flatwoods, sloughs, pond margins, ditches, and disturbed low-lying areas. It flowers mainly from summer into fall, and its flower heads provide resources for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
